```

If this file is missing or you suspect it's stale (e.g. after `kubeadm certs renew`), re-fetch it — see
`docs/ansible.md` or `docs/day2-operations.md` ("Rotating Kubernetes Certificates").

Note: `kubectl get nodes` shows `host1.lab.local` / `host2.lab.local` / `host3.lab.local` — the OS
hostname kubelet registers under, not the bare `host1`/`host2`/`host3` used elsewhere in this repo
(Ansible inventory, `hosts.csv`). Any `kubectl label`/`taint`/`describe node` command needs the
`.lab.local` suffix.

## SSH to the hosts directly

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10   # host1, control-plane
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.20   # host2, worker
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.30   # host3, worker
```

`foo` is the kickstart-created user (root login is locked, key-only auth, passwordless sudo via
`%wheel`). Add an SSH config `Host` block if typing the key path every time is annoying:

```
Host host1 host2 host3
  User foo
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab
```

Prefer fixing things through the repo (Ansible/manifests) and redeploying over ad hoc SSH changes — see
### 1. Update the target version

In `ansible/group_vars/all.yml`:
```yaml
kubernetes_version: "1.32"
```

### 2. Upgrade the control plane (host1)

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10

# Update the repo to the new minor version (already done via group_vars + Ansible)
# Or manually edit /etc/yum.repos.d/kubernetes.repo baseurl to v1.32

# Upgrade kubeadm
sudo dnf install -y --disableexcludes=kubernetes kubelet-1.32.* kubectl-1.32.*
sudo dnf versionlock delete kubelet kubectl
sudo dnf versionlock add kubelet kubectl
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart kubelet
```

### 3. Upgrade each worker (one at a time)

```bash
# From your local machine — drain the node
kubectl drain host2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

# SSH into the worker
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.20
sudo dnf install -y --disableexcludes=kubernetes kubeadm-1.32.* kubelet-1.32.* kubectl-1.32.*
sudo dnf versionlock delete kubeadm kubelet kubectl
sudo dnf versionlock add kubeadm kubelet kubectl
sudo kubeadm upgrade node
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart kubelet

# From local — uncordon
kubectl uncordon host2
```

Repeat for `host3` (10.10.10.30).

---

## Rotating Kubernetes Certificates

Certificates created by kubeadm expire after 1 year. Check expiry:

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10
sudo kubeadm certs check-expiration
```

Renew all certs:
```bash
sudo kubeadm certs renew all
sudo systemctl restart kubelet

# Regenerate kubeconfig (new cert embedded)
sudo cp /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf.bak
sudo kubeadm kubeconfig user --client-name admin > /tmp/admin.conf
sudo mv /tmp/admin.conf /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
```

Then re-fetch the kubeconfig locally:
```bash
scp -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10:/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf clusters/homelab/kubeconfig
```

---

## Adding a Worker Node

There's no VM layer to provision through Terraform anymore — a new node means new physical hardware:

ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@<host-ip> sudo reboot
# Wait for node to come back
kubectl uncordon <node>
```

Verify the host's boot order still prioritizes the local disk before rebooting anything with PXE enabled
— `bare-metal/README.md` documents the host2 reinstall-loop incident this caused once already.

---

## Backing Up etcd

kubeadm clusters store all cluster state in etcd on the control plane (host1).

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10

sudo ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).db \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

# Verify
sudo ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /tmp/etcd-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).db --write-out=table
```

Copy the snapshot off the node:
```bash
scp -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10:/tmp/etcd-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).db ./backups/
```

---

## Rebuilding the Cluster from Scratch

There's no VM layer to tear down/recreate — "from scratch" means re-running kubeadm on the same hosts:

```bash
# Reset kubeadm state on every host (control plane first, then workers)
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10 sudo kubeadm reset -f
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.20 sudo kubeadm reset -f
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.30 sudo kubeadm reset -f

# Re-bootstrap
cd ansible

lines: # Storage — Longhorn
-Longhorn provides distributed block storage across all three nodes (host1 is untainted/schedulable too,
-not etcd-only — see `docs/ansible.md`). It is the default `StorageClass`.
+Longhorn provides distributed block storage across the two **worker** nodes, host1 and host3. host2 is the
+dedicated control-plane and keeps the `NoSchedule` taint, which Longhorn's DaemonSets don't tolerate — so no
+Longhorn manager/CSI pods run there and host2's LV sits idle (see `docs/ansible.md`). It is the default
+`StorageClass`.
## How it Works
| Host | LV size | Notes |
| host1 | 800 GB | 1TB NVMe, ~846GB was free in the VG |
-| host2 | 380 GB | 512GB SATA SSD, ~397GB was free in the VG |

-| host3 | 380 GB | 512GB NVMe, ~390GB was free in the VG — **NIC currently links at only 100 Mb/s**, fix the cable/switch port before relying on this node for replica placement, replication over 100 Mb will bottleneck |

+| host2 | 380 GB | 512GB SATA SSD, ~397GB was free in the VG — **unused by Longhorn** while host2 is the tainted control-plane (carved anyway so it can become a storage worker again without a layout change) |
+| host3 | 380 GB | 512GB NVMe, ~390GB was free in the VG — runs on a USB 2.5/1GbE adapter (onboard NIC is faulty, 100 Mb/s only), so replication runs at full link speed |
-With `defaultReplicaCount: 2` (`clusters/homelab/infrastructure/longhorn.yml`) across three nodes, every
-volume is replicated onto two of the three — one node going down does not cause data loss.
+With `defaultReplicaCount: 2` (`clusters/homelab/infrastructure/longhorn.yml`) across the two storage nodes,
+every volume has one replica on host1 and one on host3 — one node going down does not cause data loss, but
+the volume stays `Degraded` until that node comes back (there's no third storage node to rebuild onto).
## Using Longhorn (PVCs)
automatically when the replica comes back.
- Disk pressure: Longhorn reserves `storageMinimalAvailablePercentage: 10` — it will stop scheduling new
replicas when less than 10% disk is free.
-- host3's degraded NIC link (100 Mb/s instead of 1 Gb/s) will slow replica rebuilds/writes to that node
-  specifically — worth fixing before leaning on this cluster for anything storage-heavy.
+- host3's onboard NIC is faulty (100 Mb/s); the USB adapter carrying its static IP is what makes
+  replication fast. If host3 ever falls back to `enp2s0` (e.g. after a reinstall, before the `usb-eth`
+  NetworkManager profile is recreated), replica writes/rebuilds to it will crawl.

# bare-metal-hmlab

Provisioning automatisé du homelab sur mini PC, via un GL.iNet Opal
(GL-SFT1200) en réseau de provisioning isolé, sans clé USB.

Fleet actuelle : **host1, host2, host3 - tous en Rocky Linux 9**, via
kickstart. Simplifié depuis une approche mixte Proxmox/Rocky qui s'est
avérée plus fragile (installeur Proxmox plus gros, dépendance à une clé
USB sur l'Opal, etc.) - Rocky/Anaconda est plus simple et plus fiable à
netbooter.

## Comment ça marche

1. L'Opal est reconfiguré en routeur isolé (LAN `10.10.10.0/24`, WAN uplinké
   vers le réseau domestique pour l'accès internet pendant l'install).
2. Le host boote en PXE (à activer dans son BIOS/UEFI).
3. `dnsmasq` sur l'Opal reconnaît chaque mini PC par adresse MAC
   (réservations statiques dans `router/dnsmasq-provisioning.conf`,
   source de vérité : `hosts.csv`) et chaîne vers iPXE.
4. iPXE (`router/boot.ipxe`) route par MAC vers le bon kickstart, puis va
   chercher le kernel/initrd Rocky et le kickstart directement en HTTPS
   (mirror officiel Rocky + ce repo GitHub) - rien de volumineux stocké
   sur les 128MB de flash de l'Opal, aucune clé USB nécessaire.
5. Anaconda installe selon le kickstart correspondant : partitionnement,
   hostname, IP statique, paquets, post-install.

## Après une install réussie : retirer le host du dispatch PXE

Le boot PXE lui-même ne redéclenche pas une réinstall à chaque reboot — un
firmware normal essaie le disque local en premier et ne retombe sur le
moment de la mise en place) - elle peut changer à chaque renouvellement de
bail DHCP. Fixer une réservation DHCP statique pour la MAC de l'Opal
(`94:83:c4:60:84:c0`) sur le routeur domestique pour que ça ne casse pas
plus tard - ce n'est pas gérable depuis ce repo, c'est côté routeur
domestique.**

## Tailscale (accès depuis n'importe où, sans dépendre du tunnel WireGuard)

Le tunnel WireGuard ci-dessus ne fonctionne que depuis le réseau domestique (le Mac doit pouvoir joindre
le WAN de l'Opal). Pour un accès depuis n'importe où sans dépendre de ça, `host1` fait office de "subnet
router" Tailscale pour `10.10.10.0/24` - annoncé via `ansible/roles/tailscale/` (playbook dédié
`ansible/playbooks/tailscale.yml`, groupe `tailscale_router` dans l'inventaire), gardé séparé de
`bootstrap.yml`.

**Pourquoi `host1` et pas l'Opal directement** : l'Opal tourne sur un SoC Siflower SF19A28 avec seulement
128 Mo de RAM/flash (target OpenWrt `siflower-1806`, cf. plus haut) - support Tailscale incertain sur ce
matériel. `host1` (Rocky Linux 9, x86_64, 32 Go RAM) a un paquet RPM officiel et zéro contrainte.

The branch `control-plane-host2` is ready for review, with 4 local commits. Nothing was pushed, `main` was not touched, and nothing on the hosts or cluster was changed. My only live access was read-only: `kubectl get nodes/ds`, reading `admin.conf` and reading `/etc/hosts` on host1. `ansible-playbook --syntax-check` passes on `bootstrap.yml` and `tailscale.yml`, and `terraform validate` passes in `terraform/cluster-bootstrap` (after `init -backend=false`; `fmt -check` is clean). The playbook itself has not been run, so the new tasks are untested against a real host.

**Worktree:** /Users/maximepatry/projects/k8s-homelab/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac05033566839842a

**Commits (oldest first):**
1. `4a94b4e` Pin kubelet --node-ip to the host's LAN address (your uncommitted main-tree change, copied verbatim)
2. `64f1efd` Document host3's USB NIC workaround instead of "fix the cable"
3. `da684bb` Move the control-plane to host2 behind a stable API endpoint name
4. `5ec0f3b` Update docs and homelab-engineer skill for the host2 control-plane

**Design decisions:**
- **Endpoint:** `kubeadm init` now gets `--control-plane-endpoint=k8s-api.lab.local:6443`, `--apiserver-advertise-address={{ ansible_host }}` and `--apiserver-cert-extra-sans=k8s-api.lab.local,<cp IP>`. The common role adds `<cp IP> k8s-api.lab.local` to `/etc/hosts` on every node. The IP comes from the first host in the `control_plane` group, not hardcoded.
- **kube-vip:** I didn't use it. With one control-plane it adds a static pod, an extra IP and ARP behaviour but no availability; the DNS name gives the same "move later without a rebuild" property. This is explained in commit 3.
- **Mac kubeconfig:** the control-plane role now writes `clusters/homelab/kubeconfig` with `server:` rewritten to `https://10.10.10.20:6443`. That IP is in the cert's SANs, so the Mac needs no `/etc/hosts` entry. It uses slurp + copy so reruns stay at 0 changes.
- **Cilium `k8sServiceHost`:** set to `10.10.10.20` (an IP, on purpose) in both `terraform/cluster-bootstrap/main.tf` and `clusters/homelab/infrastructure/cilium.yml`, which agree. I kept the IP because pods can't count on resolving a name that only exists in the nodes' `/etc/hosts` while the CNI is coming up. `helm_release.cilium` is kept.
- **Taint:** the old task that untainted host1 is gone. host2 keeps the standard `NoSchedule` taint, and the role puts it back if it's missing. On the live cluster I checked that cilium, cilium-envoy, metallb-speaker and node-exporter all tolerate it.

**Files changed:**
- `ansible/inventory/hosts.yml`: host2 is control_plane, host1 + host3 are workers; Tailscale stays on host1.
- `ansible/inventory/group_vars/all.yml`: new endpoint variables (name, port, IP derived from the inventory).
- `ansible/inventory/group_vars/control_plane.yml`: added a comment; `kubeadm_init_extra_args` was unused before and is now appended to `kubeadm init`.
- `ansible/inventory/host_vars/host2.yml`: comment that its Longhorn LV is idle while it's tainted.
- `ansible/inventory/host_vars/host3.yml`: the "fix the cable" comment now describes the USB adapter fix (onboard port faulty, PXE still via `enp2s0`).
- `ansible/roles/common/tasks/main.yml`: adds the `/etc/hosts` entry for `k8s-api.lab.local`.
- `ansible/roles/control-plane/tasks/main.yml`: new init flags, kubeconfig rewritten to the IP, untaint replaced by keeping the taint.
- `ansible/roles/kubeadm/tasks/main.yml`: the kubelet `--node-ip` fix from the main tree.
- `ansible/roles/worker/tasks/main.yml`: comment only (the join command now targets the endpoint name).
- `terraform/cluster-bootstrap/main.tf`: `k8sServiceHost` is now 10.10.10.20, with the reason for using the IP.
- `clusters/homelab/infrastructure/cilium.yml`: `k8sServiceHost` is now 10.10.10.20.
- `README.md`: hardware table, host3 NIC note, the new roles, bootstrap text and network diagram.
- `docs/ansible.md`: inventory, the new variables, an "API endpoint" section and role descriptions.
- `docs/architecture.md`: Kubernetes-layer diagram and the reasoning for host2.
- `docs/storage.md`: Longhorn now spans host1 + host3 only; host3 USB NIC.
- `docs/cluster-admin.md`: SSH role labels, and a note that the Mac needs no `/etc/hosts` entry.
- `docs/day2-operations.md`: control-plane upgrade, etcd backup and cert steps now point at host2; worker drain example uses host1; reset order; kubeconfig re-fetch goes through Ansible.
- `.claude/skills/homelab-engineer/SKILL.md`: fleet table, cluster section (endpoint, which places still use the IP, taint and DaemonSets) and history line.
- `bare-metal/README.md` (French): a docs-only section on the k8s roles and host3's USB NIC.
- `bare-metal/hosts.csv`: comment lines only (the host3 MAC is the onboard port, used for PXE). No PXE, dnsmasq or kickstart files touched.

**What the rebuild operator must do or check:**
- Run `kubeadm reset` on all three hosts first. The init task is skipped if `/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf` exists, so a leftover file on host2 would silently skip init.
- The fetched kubeconfig changes server from 10.10.10.10 to 10.10.10.20 and is regenerated on each bootstrap run. Terraform reads the same file, so run bootstrap before `terraform apply`.
- The `cilium.yml` change does nothing until it's pushed to `main` on GitHub; ArgoCD only syncs from there. Until then it would put the old 10.10.10.10 value back after adopting the release. Merge and push before or during the Terraform bootstrap.
- No Mac `/etc/hosts` change is needed, unless someone `scp`s a raw `admin.conf` by hand.
- The old host1 node object and Longhorn/ArgoCD state all go away in the rebuild, so existing PVC data on Longhorn is lost unless backed up.

**Unsure or deliberately left alone:**
- **Longhorn on host2:** its DaemonSets don't tolerate the taint, so the 380 GB LV there is carved but unused. With replica count 2, volumes now live only on host1 + host3 and stay Degraded while either is down. I kept the storage role on host2 rather than excluding it.
- **MetalLB:** kubeadm labels control-plane nodes `exclude-from-external-load-balancers`, so host2 won't announce LoadBalancer IPs. That's intended, but I haven't verified it on a fresh cluster.
- **Moving the control-plane later:** the docs say the name makes a move possible without a rebuild (join a new control-plane, repoint the name, remove the old one). That still needs a manual cert/etcd step and is not a one-variable change. The Cilium value in two places and the kubeconfig IP must also be updated by hand on any move.
- **host3 recovery:** after a PXE reinstall the `usb-eth` profile has to be recreated manually; this is documented, not automated.
- **Not reviewed:** the existing upgrade steps in `docs/day2-operations.md` look incomplete (no `kubeadm upgrade apply` shown for the control-plane). I only changed the hosts and IPs.
- `docs/ci-cd.md`, `docs/networking.md` and the Homepage/MetalLB/ingress manifests had nothing tied to host1 as control-plane, so they're unchanged. `bare-metal/README.md` keeps its existing `10.10.10.10` references because those are Tailscale on host1, which is correct.
